content: 1. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The net exposure of ivacaftor at steady-state is not expected to exceed levels seen with monotherapy at 150 mg every 12 hours. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already on lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg) for the first week to allow for steady-state induction effects of lumacaftor. After this period, resume the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is needed for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the dose to 5 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Ritonavir may increase or decrease levels of lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Decrease maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, ritonavir increases the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Mavorixafor increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution when co-administering mavorixafor with sensitive P-gp substrates, as minimal substrate concentration changes may lead to serious adverse effects. 8. Ritonavir increases levels of meperidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, ritonavir also decreases mestranol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as this may result in contraceptive failure. Use additional or alternative contraceptive methods. 10. Ritonavir decreases the effects of metformin through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but may also decrease methadone effects by inducing its metabolism or the P-glycoprotein pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of methamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, methylprednisolone decreases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of mexiletine toxicity (e.g., nausea, dizziness, cardiac arrhythmias). Therapeutic concentration monitoring is recommended if available. Reduce mexiletine doses as required. 17. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely for QTc interval prolongation. 20. Ritonavir decreases the effects of miglitol through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 21. Co-administration of ritonavir and mipomersen may increase the toxicity of either drug due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 22. Mirabegron increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ritonavir increases levels of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4 (a cytotoxic component of the antibody-drug conjugate), increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Mitotane decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 26. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters. Monitor closely for adverse reactions, as increased plasma concentrations of momelotinib may occur. 27. Ritonavir increases levels of mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity, including the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. 28. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Nafcillin decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ritonavir increases levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 31. Ritonavir decreases the effects of nateglinide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nebivolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Nefazodone increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Nelfinavir increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. No dosage adjustment is required. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Nevirapine decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir also increases nevirapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nicardipine also increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Nifedipine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but decreases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Nilotinib increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ritonavir increases levels of nintedanib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. 42. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Ritonavir decreases olanzapine levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 48. Ritonavir and olodaterol (inhaled) both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 49. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Ritonavir and ondansetron both increase the QTc interval. Avoid use in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant medications that prolong the QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. Ritonavir also increases ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Orlistat decreases ritonavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 52. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the dose of osilodrostat (a CYP3A4 substrate) by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 53. Ritonavir increases levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Oxcarbazepine decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of oxymorphone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ozanimod by mechanisms involving CYP2C8 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of ozanimod (a CYP2C8 substrate) with strong CYP2C8 inhibitors increases the exposure of its active metabolites (CC112273 and CC1084037), which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Both ozanimod and ritonavir prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs.
